road.name: Chiwawa River Road / Forest Road 6200
road.status: Paved becoming gravel/dirt roughly 11 miles in, rough for the final ~12 miles to Trinity Trailhead
road.driveNote: Same access as the East Ridge — see that route for full driving directions.
road.seasonalGate: Unplowed in winter; winter access uses a ~21-mile unplowed road from Fish Lake Sno-Park

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (Forest Road 6200)
road.status: Paved near Lake Wenatchee, transitioning to rough washboard gravel/dirt for roughly the final 12 miles to the Trinity/Phelps Creek trailheads; passable to most vehicles in dry conditions but slow going for low-clearance cars.
road.driveNote: From Leavenworth: US-2 west ~15 mi to Coles Corner, WA-207 north 4.4 mi, then Chiwawa River Rd (FR 6200) up-valley to the Trinity/Phelps Creek trailheads.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (Forest Road 6200 / FR-62)
road.status: Decent gravel for roughly the first 11 miles from WA-207, then narrow, rough, and high-clearance-recommended for the final ~12 miles to Trinity Trailhead; sections beyond Goose Creek have been closed in some years by flood damage and wildfire activity.
road.driveNote: From US-2 near Coles Corner, take WA-207 north about 4.4 miles, turn onto Chiwawa Loop Road, then follow signs onto Chiwawa River Road/FR-6200 for about 23 miles to Trinity Trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: Typically snow-closed in winter/spring; verify current status with the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest before driving, as fire and flood closures have occurred in recent seasons.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road / Phelps Creek Road
road.status: Unpaved, rough and washboarded; high-clearance vehicle recommended
road.driveNote: Long gravel forest roads to the Phelps Creek / Chiwawa trailheads

access.fees: None — no climbing fee (National Forest wilderness, not Mount Rainier NP)
access.closures: Little Giant Fire Closure Order 06-17-07-2026-33, effective 14 Aug 2026 through 31 Oct 2026, closes FR 6200 (Chiwawa River Rd), FR 6211 (Phelps Creek Rd), Phelps Creek Trail #1511, Leroy Creek Trail #1512 AND the Entiat River alternate (Entiat River Rd/FR 5100, Cottonwood Campground, Entiat River Trail #1400). Fire is 147,537 acres, 21% contained as of 25 Aug 2026.
access.landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Glacier Peak Wilderness vicinity)
access.land_manager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Chiwawa/Entiat Ranger Districts) — Glacier Peak Wilderness
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at some trailheads (fee day-use sites) — $5/day or $30/year.
access.passRequired: None at the Phelps Creek Trailhead - the Forest Service lists it as a no-fee site, so no Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is needed to park. The Glacier Peak Wilderness permit is free and self-issued at the register.

overnight_permit.what: Free self-issue Glacier Peak Wilderness permit
overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the trailhead kiosk (Phelps Creek, Trinity, Entiat River, or the Holden trailheads). Holden Village and its access road are closed to hikers through at least summer 2026.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) to Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211)
road.status: Gravel forest road, rough in sections, high-clearance recommended
road.driveNote: From US-2/SR-207 near Lake Wenatchee, follow Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) about 22 miles, then turn right on Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211) and continue ~2.3-2.5 miles to the trailhead (3,500 ft).
road.seasonalGate: Typically snow-free and drivable late May/June through fall; subject to storm-damage closures - check current Okanogan-Wenatchee NF alerts before driving

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) to Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211)
road.status: Gravel forest road, rough in sections, high-clearance recommended
road.driveNote: From US-2/SR-207 near Lake Wenatchee, follow Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) about 22 miles, then turn right on Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211) and continue ~2.3-2.5 miles to the trailhead (3,500 ft).
road.seasonalGate: Typically snow-free and drivable late May/June through fall; subject to storm-damage closures - check current Okanogan-Wenatchee NF alerts before driving

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) to Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211)
road.status: Paved/gravel Chiwawa Loop Road transitions to gravel/dirt FR 6200 beyond about mile 11, then FR 6211 for the final ~2.3 miles — rough and rutted, not suitable for low-clearance vehicles; roughly 14 miles of rough dirt/gravel total.
road.driveNote: From Leavenworth: US-2 west ~15 mi to Coles Corner, WA-207 north ~4.4 mi, then Chiwawa Loop Road to Chiwawa River Rd/FR 6200 for ~22 mi, then FR 6211 ~2.3 mi to the Phelps Creek Trailhead (3,500 ft).
road.seasonalGate: Typically snowed shut from late fall through spring; opening date varies by year and is further affected by storm-damage closures — check Wenatchee River Ranger District road/trail alerts before driving.

road.name: Entiat River Road (County Rd 19 -> FR 51 at mile 27 -> unpaved FR 5100 at mile 34)
road.status: Paved to about mile 34, then gravel FR 5100 to the trailhead; single-lane sections with pullouts near the old washout/burn area.
road.driveNote: 37.3 miles from the town of Entiat (reached via US-97A) to the Entiat River Trailhead at 3,150 ft - this is a standard drive-to trailhead, not boat/ferry access.
road.seasonalGate: Winter gate near the Entiat Sno-Park (~mile 25); reopening date varies by year, sometimes into May.

road.name: Entiat River Road (FR 51, becomes FR 5100)
road.status: Paved for roughly the first 34 miles west from the town of Entiat; the final several miles past Cottonwood Campground to the Entiat River Trailhead are gravel and can be rough or washed out.
road.driveNote: From the town of Entiat on US-97A, head west on the Entiat River Road (FR 51) and follow it about 38 miles to its end at the Entiat River Trailhead (~3,150 ft), a short distance past where the pavement ends at Cottonwood Campground.
road.seasonalGate: Not formally gated, but the upper gravel section is not reliably passenger-car-friendly until spring grading/washout repairs are done, and the road can be snowed in during winter.

road.name: FR 5606 (final 3 miles) via Entiat River Road/County Rd 19 to FR 51
road.status: Mostly graded gravel; generally passable for passenger cars in dry conditions with a couple of rough or dry-crossing sections, though high clearance is recommended. East-Cascades forest roads here wash out periodically — check the current road report with the Entiat Ranger District before driving.
road.driveNote: From the town of Entiat on US-97A, follow Entiat River Road (County Rd 19) north/west; it becomes FR 51 around mile 27, continue to mile 32.3, then turn onto FR 5606 and drive 3 more miles to its end at the North Fork Entiat Trailhead (3,940 ft).

road.name: Entiat River Road (County Road 19 → Forest Road 51) to Forest Road 5606
road.status: Paved for roughly the first 27 miles from the town of Entiat, then gravel Forest Road 51 to the FR 5606 junction at about 32.3 miles, then gravel FR 5606 north for a final 3 miles to the trailhead (~35.3 miles total); subject to intermittent washout/landslide damage.
road.driveNote: From US-97A in Entiat, follow Entiat River Road/Forest Road 51 about 32.3 miles, then turn right (north) onto Forest Road 5606 for a final 3 miles to its end at the North Fork Entiat Trailhead (el. ~3,940 ft), about 35.3 miles total. Expect washboard gravel and creek-crossing damage on the upper miles; high-clearance recommended, and a trailer ban may be in effect if a slide bypass is active — verify current status before driving up.

road.name: Entiat River Road (Chelan County Rd 19, becomes Forest Road 51 at mile 27), then Forest Road 5606 for the North Fork Entiat Trailhead
road.status: Paved for roughly the first 27 miles from Entiat, then gravel FR 51/5606; the road has a history of multi-year closures from storm and flood damage — verify current status before driving.
road.driveNote: From Entiat, follow Entiat River Road north about 32.3 miles to FR 5606, then 3 miles to its end at the North Fork Entiat Trailhead (3,940 ft); or continue on FR 51 to the Entiat River/Cottonwood Camp Trailhead for the classic Entiat River Trail approach into Pinnacle Creek.

road.name: Entiat River Road to Forest Road 5606 (North Fork Entiat Road)
road.status: Paved for ~32.5 miles, then gravel FR 5606 for ~3 switchbacking miles to the trailhead (~3,700 ft)
road.driveNote: Day-use only at the trailhead; check current Okanogan-Wenatchee NF alerts for fire or storm-damage closures. Alternate approach via Lucerne requires a Lake Chelan boat/ferry shuttle.

access.fees: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass for trailhead parking
access.landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Entiat Ranger District
access.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass / America the Beautiful Pass

overnight_permit.what: Free self-issue Glacier Peak Wilderness permit
overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the North Fork Entiat, Entiat River or Phelps Creek trailhead kiosk.

road.name: Lucerne Landing-Holden Village Road (FR 8301)
road.status: Closed to public vehicle and foot traffic per Forest Order #755
road.driveNote: No public road access; drive to Chelan, ferry to Lucerne, shuttle to Holden Village.

access.fees: Lake Chelan Boat Company ferry fare plus Holden Village shuttle fee.
access.permit: No backcountry permit required; register at Holden Village's Hike Haus.
access.closures: FR 8301 corridor closed to public per Forest Order #755.
access.landManager: USDA Forest Service - Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Chelan Ranger District (Glacier Peak Wilderness)
access.passRequired: Not applicable to the boat-based approach.

road.name: Lucerne Landing-Holden Village Road (FR 8301)
road.status: Closed to public vehicle and foot traffic per Forest Order #755
road.driveNote: Standard approach is by ferry to Lucerne then Holden Village shuttle; avoid the FA team's atypical 32-mile bike/hike approach, which was necessitated by closures in 2013.

access.fees: Lake Chelan Boat Company ferry fare plus Holden Village shuttle fee (standard approach).
access.permit: No backcountry permit required; register at Holden Village's Hike Haus.
access.closures: FR 8301 corridor closed to public per Forest Order #755.
access.landManager: USDA Forest Service - Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Chelan Ranger District (Glacier Peak Wilderness)
access.passRequired: Not applicable to the boat-based approach.

road.name: Holden Village Road (Lucerne Landing to Holden Village)
road.status: Gravel shuttle road; no direct public road access — reached only via Lake Chelan ferry to Lucerne, then the village shuttle bus
road.driveNote: There is no drive-in trailhead. Ferry to Lucerne Landing, then an 11-mile gravel road with 12 switchbacks by Holden Village shuttle bus to reach Holden Village and the Railroad Creek Trail.

access.fees: Northwest Forest Pass $5/day or $30/annual at the Chiwawa-side trailheads; the wilderness permit itself is free; the Lady of the Lake ferry to Lucerne/Holden Village charges its own separate fare
access.rules: Leave No Trace; no camping within 200 ft of the Lyman Lakes shoreline; wilderness group size limit is 12 people/stock combined; pack out all trash — no services in the wilderness
access.permit: Free, self-issued wilderness permit at the trailhead register — no reservation or quota required
access.closures: Chiwawa River Road (FSR 6200) is closed to vehicles from Atkinson Flat Campground north to Trinity under USFS closure order #06-17-07-2026-11 (effective 5/20/2026 through at least 12/31/2027, no reopening estimate) after December 2025 storm damage — this currently blocks vehicle access to both the Phelps Creek and Trinity trailheads. Check fs.usda.gov/r06/okanogan-wenatchee/alerts or call (509) 548-2550 before planning a trip via those trailheads; the Holden Village/Railroad Creek approach is unaffected
access.landManager: Glacier Peak Wilderness, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest — Wenatchee River Ranger District administers the Chiwawa River Rd/Phelps Creek and Trinity approaches; Chelan Ranger District administers the Holden Village/Railroad Creek approach
access.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass ($5/day or $30/annual) required to park at the Phelps Creek and Trinity trailheads; not required for the Holden Village/ferry approach

overnight_permit.what: Free self-issue Glacier Peak Wilderness permit
overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the trailhead kiosk (Phelps Creek, Trinity, Entiat River, or the Holden trailheads). Holden Village and its access road are closed to hikers through at least summer 2026.

road.name: Index-Galena Road (FR 63) from Index, or Beckler Road (FR 65) via Jack Pass as the current detour
road.status: Direct Index-Galena Road access is closed to vehicles (~MP 10–14 washed out since Dec 2025); current access is via the Beckler Road/Jack Pass detour.
road.driveNote: From US-2 near Index, FR 63 runs north along the North Fork Skykomish River, but its final miles to the trailhead are currently impassable to vehicles. The working detour is US-2 to Beckler Road (FR 65) near Skykomish, ~12.5 mi to Jack Pass, then ~1.8–2.5 mi on FR 63 to the Blanca Lake Trailhead — gravel, rough in spots, roughly 45 minutes longer than the old Index route; low-clearance cars and RVs can struggle.
road.seasonalGate: The Beckler Road/Jack Pass detour closes seasonally with snow and is typically not reliably open until early summer.

road.name: Mountain Loop Highway to Barlow Pass Trailhead, then the gated Monte Cristo Road (non-motorized)
road.driveNote: Paved the full 34 miles from Granite Falls to Barlow Pass Trailhead. Beyond the trailhead, the Monte Cristo Road is gravel, gated, and closed to motor vehicles — hike or bike the 4 miles to the townsite. Alternate approach to Blanca Lake: from Index, take Index-Galena Road/FR 63 roughly 13.8 miles paved plus 2 miles gravel to the Blanca Lake Trailhead.

road.name: Lake Cushman Rd / North Fork Skokomish Rd (becomes Forest Road 24)
road.status: Closed as of 2026 due to the Bear Gulch Fire closure order (FR 24 gated near milepost 10.5–14.5; the Staircase entrance is also closed) — verify current status before driving out.
road.driveNote: When open: from US-101 in Hoodsport, follow Lake Cushman Rd/N. Fork Skokomish Rd about 15–16 miles to the Staircase Ranger Station (~850 ft) at the NW end of Lake Cushman.

access.fees: Olympic NP entrance: $30/vehicle or $15/person for 7 days, $55 annual Olympic pass (nps.gov/olym, 2026 rates). Overnight wilderness camping permit for Flapjack Lakes (a quota/limited-entry area including Gladys Divide) costs a $6 Recreation.gov reservation fee plus $8/person/night (16+, free under 16); summer-season (May 15–Oct 15) permits release April 15 and this is one of the park's highest-demand backcountry zones.
access.notes: No separate climbing cost-recovery fee like Mount Rainier’s $82 — only the standard entrance fee and wilderness camping permit apply.
access.rules: Flapjack Lakes is a quota/limited-use area — no same-day walk-up permits once the season sells out; groups capped at 12, parties of 7+ must use designated group campsites; stick to your permitted itinerary except in emergencies.
access.permit: NPS wilderness/backcountry permit required for any overnight camping at Flapjack Lakes or Gladys Divide, booked in advance on Recreation.gov (Wilderness Information Center, 360-565-3100); no separate climbing permit is needed once past the park boundary into the Mount Skokomish Wilderness.
access.closures: IMPORTANT (current as of mid-2026): the entire standard approach — Staircase entrance, North Fork Skokomish River Trail, Flapjack Lakes Trail, and the nearby Mildred Lakes Trail (an alternate approach) — is closed following the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire on the slopes above Lake Cushman (fire fully contained Nov 12, 2025, but rockfall/treefall/landslide hazard remains in the burn scar). NPS and Olympic National Forest closure orders remain in effect (through at least Oct 1, 2026 per USFS order 06-09-25-11); Lake Cushman Rd/Forest Road 24 access is also closed. There is currently no legal approach to Mount Cruiser via Flapjack Lakes — check NPS Olympic 'Fire Conditions and Updates' and Olympic National Forest alerts before planning a trip.
access.landManager: Approach trail (Staircase, North Fork Skokomish River Trail, Flapjack Lakes Trail, Gladys Divide) is within Olympic National Park (NPS); the summit and Sawtooth Ridge itself sit just south of the park boundary in the Mount Skokomish Wilderness, Olympic National Forest.
access.land_manager: U.S. Forest Service -- Mount Skokomish Wilderness, Olympic National Forest (summit/Sawtooth Ridge); the approach trail via Staircase lies within Olympic National Park.
access.parking_pass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
access.passRequired: NPS entrance pass (or America the Beautiful pass) for vehicle/individual entry at the Staircase entrance station; no Northwest Forest Pass needed since the trailhead itself is inside the National Park boundary.

overnight_permit.what: Olympic National Park wilderness permit, reserved in advance, per-night fee
overnight_permit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov before the trip; there are no same-day walk-up permits. Bear canisters are required at Flapjack Lakes, and the Staircase trails are closed after the Bear Gulch Fire, so check status first.

road.name: Staircase Road (North Fork Skokomish Road, off US-101 at Hoodsport)
road.status: Open — FS-24 and the Staircase developed area reopened 8 July 2026 after a year-long closure following the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire
road.driveNote: With Staircase closed, the Duckabush Trailhead (off US-101 near Brinnon) is the currently viable paved, drive-to access point for this peak, via Duckabush Trail #803 toward Marmot Lake.
road.seasonalGate: Open; the road itself is no longer gated for the fire. Verify before travel.

road.name: North Fork Skokomish / Staircase Road
road.status: Pavement ends ~1.7 mi onto FR-24 from Hoodsport, then ~3.7 mi of gravel to the Staircase Ranger Station/trailhead. As of mid-2026, the developed Staircase area reopened July 8, 2026 after a year-long closure from the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire, but surrounding wilderness trails - including the Flapjack Lakes/North Fork Skokomish Trail used for this route's approach - remain closed for post-fire repair; verify current status before attempting.
road.driveNote: Access is via the Staircase area of Olympic National Park (North Fork Skokomish). The Staircase developed area (road, campground, ranger station) was closed by the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire and is scheduled to reopen 7/8/2026, but the Flapjack Lakes and North Fork Skokomish trails beyond the developed area remain closed for hazard mitigation as of mid-2026 — confirm current road AND trail status before the trip.
road.seasonalGate: Typically snow-affected/closed November-May in normal (non-fire-closure) years.

access.fees: $8/person/night camping fee + $6 non-refundable reservation fee for any overnight wilderness permit; a $45 annual Wilderness Pass covers per-night fees for 12 months.
access.permit: A wilderness/backcountry camping permit is required year-round for any overnight stay, booked through Recreation.gov; Flapjack Lakes/Gladys Divide is a fixed-capacity quota area.
access.closures: Campfires are prohibited above 3,500 ft; within the Flapjack Lakes/Gladys Divide quota zone, deviating from your permitted itinerary is not allowed except in emergencies.
access.passRequired: NPS wilderness camping permit (Recreation.gov) required for overnight stays; a day climb does not need a wilderness permit but a park entrance fee/pass applies.
